algorithm: Multi-modal constrained shortest path: a deterministic label-setting Dijkstra variant over a 90-region time-expanded graph. Each state is (region, mode, link_entry_state). Edge relaxation uses a non-negative scalar cost = travel_time + mode_change_penalty + congestion_delay + control/treaty_delay. Ties are broken by a fixed total order (cost, then arrival_tick, then link_id, then mode_rank, then region_id) so results are bit-for-bit reproducible across runs/machines. Priority queue is a binary min-heap keyed by that total order; no floating point, all costs are integer ticks (e.g. 1 tick = 1 hour). A single Node owns the Router; all public calls are single-threaded on the main loop, so no locks are needed. Path reconstruction stores predecessor pointers in the settled label table. Because costs are non-negative and integer, Dijkstra optimality holds; capacity/state effects are folded into per-relaxation integer costs rather than dynamic global multipliers, preserving determinism and avoiding any unlimited global bonus.

graph.regions: 90 nodes, id 0..89, fixed stable order; adjacency lists pre-sorted by neighbor id for deterministic iteration.

link.reverse_ok: bool (rail/road/port/river usually bidirectional; mountain passes may be one-way)
link.river_direction: optional flow direction for river; upstream costs extra

mode_change.matrix: int[N][N] penalty ticks to switch from mode i to mode j at a region; diagonal 0; symmetric; fixed constants in data, never scaled globally
mode_change.node_transfer: per-region transfer time when changing mode (e.g. rail depot, port wharf)
mode_change.applied_when: only on the relaxation where incoming mode != outgoing mode

link_runtime_state.DEGRADED: time_multiplier_x100 (e.g. 150 = +50%) and capacity_multiplier_x100 (e.g. 50 = half); deterministic int math
link_runtime_state.INTERRUPTED: not traversable; skipped entirely, no fallback bonus
link_runtime_state.REPAIR: treated as INTERRUPTED until repair_done_tick; then auto-transitions to OPEN (or DEGRADED per data)
link_runtime_state.state_timeline: each link keeps a sorted list of {from_tick, state, time_mult_x100, cap_mult_x100}; lookup by current sim tick via binary search. No randomness.

capacity_model.window: capacity is per discrete tick window W (e.g. demand for the next 24 ticks is reserved at route commit)
capacity_model.usage: per-link int used_units[window] tracked by the routing manager, updated at path commit, not during search
capacity_model.edge_cost: base_time_adjusted + ceil(demand_units * congestion_factor / max(free_capacity,1)) when free_capacity > 0; edge skipped when free_capacity <= 0
capacity_model.no_global_bonus: There is no global speed multiplier or team-wide bonus. All modifiers are local, per-link, per-tick, integer, and capped by the multipliers in state timelines. Congestion can only increase cost or block; it never decreases below base_time.
capacity_model.reservation: at commit, each accepted path atomically adds demand_units to every traversed link's usage for the relevant windows; if any link lacks capacity the whole path is rejected and the search reruns with those links blocked (cache invalidated).

territory.owner: per-region int faction id, or -1 neutral
territory.transit_treaty: bool[ faction ][ faction ] matrix from game state; symmetric unless data says otherwise
territory.rule: entering a region requires owner == self, or owner == -1, or treaty[self][owner] == true; otherwise the region is impassable
territory.transit_delay: int ticks added when entering a foreign treaty region (e.g. customs), from fixed data
territory.control_of_link: optional: if either endpoint is hostile and no treaty, even an otherwise open link is blocked

cache.key: hash of (source_region, target_region, demand_units, sim_tick_window, mode_allow_mask, owner_vector, treaty_matrix_version, link_state_version, usage_vector_version)
cache.value: {path: Array[int link ids], total_cost: int, computed_at_tick: int}
cache.policy: LRU with fixed max entries (e.g. 256); deterministic eviction by (last_used_tick, insertion_seq, key)

invalidation.mechanism: monotonic version counters per class; on event bump the relevant version, and any cache entry whose key embeds that version becomes stale and is purged lazily on lookup and eagerly on bump for small maps

cache.safety: cache is pure function of key; never store mutable arrays by reference; return copies. A miss always recomputes from current state.

integration_points: Router.gd singleton (autoload) exposing func find_path(src:int, dst:int, demand:int, mode_mask:int) -> Dictionary and func commit_path(path:Dictionary) -> bool.
MapData resource loaded once from data/routes.json (or .tres): regions, links, base times, capacities, mode-change matrix, transfer times.
GameState signal bus: emit region_owner_changed, treaty_changed, link_state_changed( link_id, new_state ), repair_completed( link_id ) -> Router.invalidate(tag).
SimClock:Router uses current tick window; connect tick_window_rolled signal to invalidate window-scoped entries.
MovementOrder/planner calls Router.find_path, displays total_cost and per-link mode changes; on commit, Router reserves capacity and emits path_committed(link_ids, demand).
Save/load: serialize link state timelines, usage vectors, and version counters; cache itself is NOT serialized, it is rebuilt after load.
limits: 90 nodes * up to 5 modes => at most 450 label states; edges <= 5 per pair, so Dijkstra is O((V*M + E*M) log(V*M)) and bounded/small.
Integer-only arithmetic avoids floating drift; time multipliers use x100 fixed point with explicit floor/ceil rules.
Capacity is reserved per window, not continuous; a path spanning many windows must reserve in each and can fail in any one.
INTERRUPTED/REPAIR links are hard blockers, never rerouted with a hidden bonus; if no path exists the Router returns {found:false, reason} deterministically.
Transit treaties are binary and global per faction pair; no partial or negotiated transit is modeled.
Mountain layer is slow and capacity-limited; it is just another mode, not an always-available fallback.
No dynamic obstacle prediction; link states are taken as current at search time and a commit may fail if state changes before reservation (caller retries).
Determinism assumes all inputs (data table order, version counters, current tick) are fixed for a given call; any nondeterministic upstream data breaks reproducibility.

capacity_model.type: per-link per-tick-window integer reservation with congestion cost, no global bonus
capacity_model.formula: available = floor(capacity * cap_mult_x100 / 100) - used; if available <= 0 skip edge; else added_cost = ceil(demand * congestion_factor / available)
capacity_model.reservation: atomic at commit across all windows traversed; all-or-nothing, rollback on failure
invariants: effects are local to the link, never a global multiplier

cache.type: versioned LRU keyed by full query + state versions
cache.invalidation: bump version counters on owner/treaty/link-state/repair/tick-window/usage changes; stale entries purged on lookup and eagerly on event
cache.determinism: LRU eviction uses (last_used_tick, insertion_seq, key) total order; no wall-clock time in keys

integration_points: MovementOrder planner consumes paths and reservations
Save/load serializes state + versions, rebuilds cache
limits: capacity per discrete window, all-or-nothing commit
hard blocks for interrupted/repair and hostile territory
no unlimited global bonus or hidden fallback
no predictive state changes; caller retries on commit failure
